messages:
Samir K.: Hey team — customer reported repeated 400 errors from the embeddings endpoint when they ramp throughput. Says error message 'dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024'. Happening intermittently, more often under high load.

Lina M.: Thanks Samir. Any chance they're switching model variants during requests? That error usually means payload vectors length doesn't match model config.

Samir K.: I asked for full request/response. They sent this snippet: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"model":"embed-large-1536","input":["a","b"]}'``` Response: ```{ "error": "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024" }``` They say loads of requests succeed but ~0.6% fail during spikes.

Diego R.: Could be dynamic batching mixing requests targeted at different models on the same worker pool if routing allows multiple model sizes. Does customer use any custom routing or model aliases?

Samir K.: They said they pinned "embed-large-1536" but are on Dedicated and using an autoscaling pool.

Priya S.: Two quick hypotheses: 1) There's an optimized quantized variant with 1024 dims masquerading under the same alias (bad alias mapping). 2) A bug in the batching code that appends KV cache or padding incorrectly causing a mismatch at serialization time.

Lina M.: Can we repro locally? Diego, any way to simulate dynamic batching noise? Maybe send mixed model requests with identical alias to see if pool routes different binaries?

Diego R.: I'll spin up a small repro. Plan: run two model binaries (one 1536, one 1024) and set alias config so both respond to same model name. Then hammer concurrent embeddings with varying payload sizes. I'll capture the batch packer logs.

Samir K.: Customer provided a quick log excerpt showing: ```[2026-11-18T13:45:22Z] batch_id=abc123 packer: saw request(model=embed-large-1536, vec_len=1536)
[2026-11-18T13:45:22Z] batch_id=abc123 packer: saw request(model=embed-large-1536, vec_len=1024)
[2026-11-18T13:45:22Z] worker: serialize error: dims mismatch
``` They also pasted a prometheus graph link for tail latency spikes around the same time (links are internal).

Priya S.: That log is suspicious — packer saw both 1536 and 1024 under same model name. Could be alias misconfiguration during rollout. Samir, can you check if the customer rotated model symlinks or recently did a canary deploy?

Samir K.: They confirmed they pushed a new quantized variant yesterday and mentioned 'we updated alias mapping to point to latest for all envs' — so likely mis-mapped.

Lina M.: Two action items: 1) Ask customer to pin to the explicit model id (not alias) as immediate mitigation. Provide exact curl snippet. 2) We'll reproduce and patch packer to drop requests with mismatched dims instead of attempting to batch them. Also add debug metric `batch_mismatched_dims_total`.

Samir K.: I'll send mitigation instructions now: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"embed-large-1536-v2","input":["text1","text2"]}'``` Note: explicit model id `embed-large-1536-v2`.

Diego R.: Repro status: I could reproduce 400s when alias pointed to multiple binaries. Pack logs show interleaving: ```packer: grouping N=8; mixed_dims=[1536,1024]; serialization aborted``` With dynamic batching enabled, the packer accepted heterogeneous dims because alias check was done only at request enqueue. Fix idea: validate dims during final pack stage and refuse batch if heterogeneous.

Priya S.: Also adding a unit test for the batcher that simulates concurrent enqueues with mixed dims. And for Dedicated, we should add an alert when alias->multiple-binaries mapping occurs.

Lina M.: Quick question: should we hotfix to return 429 or 400 in these cases? 400 seems correct (bad request payload) but 409 or 422 might convey mismatch. Preference: return 400 with clearer message and increment `batch_mismatched_dims_total` so SRE can alert.

Diego R.: I'll open PR with packer validation + metric + improved error text: `dimension mismatch within batch: ensure all requests target same model variant and vector size`. Will target a canary rollout to Dedicated pools first.

Samir K.: Customer mitigation sent, they pinned model id. Customer confirmed errors dropped to 0.05% after pinning. They want root cause and permanent guard in platform.

Priya S.: Summarizing root cause: alias mapping allowed two incompatible model binaries under same name (quantized variant with different output dims). Dynamic batching combined requests under the alias causing mixed-dimension batches and serialization errors. Fixes: alias validation during model registration, batcher runtime validation, metric/alert.

Lina M.: Samir, please escalate with the customer-facing summary and ETA for the patch (Diego, estimate?).

Diego R.: ETA: PR in 3 business days, CI + canary 2 days, full rollout 1 week after approval. Will include test cases and metrics.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3847 assigned to eng-runtime. Link: internal/INC-2026-3847

Samir K.: Thanks all — I'll update the customer and move thread to resolved once patch is gated. :thumbsup:
